title: GPU microburst OOMs: KV-index leakage & fragmentation fix
creator: Ava Chen
description: Customers (hosted and dedicated) reported intermittent GPU OOMs that clustered in short bursts ("microbursts") during high-concurrency workloads. The incidents manifested as ephemeral OOMs that recovered automatically, but frequency and customer impact made this a P0. Investigation showed correlation between request microbursts, rapid KV handle churn, aggressive tombstone accumulation in the KV-index, and allocator slab fragmentation which together caused transient page saturation on GPUs. This ticket implements a runtime patch to reduce OOM frequency by coalescing KV-index tombstones during bursts, adding a lightweight ephemeral-arena fallback, and introducing preemptive allocator backpressure for failing reserve paths.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a synthetic load generator hitting hosted/dedicated endpoints with bursts: 400 concurrent requests over 30s every 5 minutes.
2) Use model variant with long context (>= 4096 tokens) to increase KV cache usage and session handle creation.
3) Observe GPU memory high-water events followed by OOMs within 10-40s of burst start.
4) Reproduce reliably on canary dedicated pool with same request pattern (saw ~3 OOMs/hour pre-fix).
investigation_notes: 11/10: Triage — customer reports from three customers (one hosted, two dedicated) all show microburst timing + increased KV-index write amplification.
11/11: Heap dump and KV-index snapshot analysis — tombstone density increases by 6x during microbursts; index compaction did not keep up under burst churn.

11/12: Allocator profiling — slab allocator shows fragmentation growth; small ephemeral allocations prevented large contiguous pages from being allocated; GPU page allocator returned ENOMEM despite aggregate free memory due to scatter.

11/12: Hypothesis — rapid creation+deletion of session KV handles creates index entropy (many small tombstones) causing compaction and allocation stalls; concurrent tombstone scans hold index locks and block reclamation leading to allocator failure under burst pressure.
11/13: Confirmed with stress harness that delaying tombstone compaction by 200ms and coalescing writes reduces allocation stalls and decreases OOM rate in controlled test by ~85%.
mitigation_actions: Immediate mitigations (11/11-11/12): enabled conservative request admission on affected dedicated clusters and applied ephemeral session TTL reduction for a subset of tenants to reduce churn.
Hotpatch (11/13): pushed runtime flag kv_index_coalesce=true to canary pool which batches tombstone writes and defers full compaction under microburst detection.

Hotfix (11/14): rolled out runtime-1.21 patch that introduces the ephemeral-arena fallback and allocator reserve probe; added preemptive backpressure when reserve probe fails (requests receive 429 with retry-after during extreme bursts instead of causing OOM).
Communication: Sent incident summaries and mitigation steps to the three affected customers; offered dedicated support windows for validation.
patch_refs: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7896 — ephemeral-arena fallback + allocator reserve probe
Commit: runtime@4f7b2a9 — allocator: preemptive reserve probe and backpressure hooks
rollout_plan: Canary (11/14): 5% of Dedicated GPU pool for 24 hours with increased tracing and OOM guard enabled.
Gradual (11/15): Move to 25% then 75% over next 24 hours if no regressions in latency or error rate.
Hosted (11/16-11/17): Apply to hosted fleet after 48h of dedicated canary stability; soft-fallback enabled to prior runtime on error.
Rollback plan: Immediate rollback to previous runtime release if >5 OOMs/hour observed in canary or 2x increase in 5xx rate.
Customer opt-in: For high-risk tenants, we offered manual canary validation windows and the ability to pin pre-fix runtime for 48h.
monitoring_changes: Added tombstone_density gauge for KV-index by tenant and global index compaction lag.
Alert: OOM_MICROBURST_HIGH when >2 OOMs in 30m on any single node (notify SRE + oncall).
Tracing: Added kv-index compaction spans to request traces for 99th percentile latency correlation.
postmortem_summary: Root cause was a compound failure mode: short, high-concurrency request bursts produced rapid KV handle churn that created a large number of small tombstones in the KV-index. The index compaction path, when contending with tombstone scans under load, held locks and prevented timely reclamation of memory pages; the slab allocator then fragmented and failed to satisfy contiguous GPU page allocations, producing transient OOMs. The runtime patch reduced OOMs from ~3/hour (canary baseline) to ~0.2/hour during production-like burst tests and reduced average GPU page allocation failures by ~92%. Customer-facing impact dropped to negligible after the full rollout; affected customers confirmed improved stability.
follow_up_tasks: ENG: Evaluate long-term KV-index redesign to tolerate high-churn workloads without compaction stalls (RFC Q1 2026).
SRE: Add tenant-level throttles that are workload-aware (action item in oncall runbook).
QA: Add microburst regression tests to nightly stress suite with both long-context and short-context models.
Product: Document tradeoffs of 429 backpressure for latency-sensitive customers and provide opt-out guidance.
Observability: Improve dashboards to show index tombstone growth as a first-class signal.
